I verified it by rendering the public page in a browser (no login). Both subprocessor entries link to the 'enabling and using web search' help article. questions.answer: No public BAA offer found, and Tavily's own terms point the other way. The MSA's DPA §1.8 (Sensitive Data) has customers warrant they won't submit HIPAA PHI without Tavily's prior written consent. The Acceptable Use Policy (updated 2026-05-05, §3 Prohibited Input) also lists HIPAA PHI. The written-consent carve-out leaves room for a negotiated arrangement, but none is documented.
questions.notes: WebFetch couldn't parse the MSA PDF; I downloaded it with curl and extracted the text locally. Nudge Security's profile (r31) shows an unsourced 'HIPAA Compliant' badge that conflicts with Tavily's terms; don't use it. The KB records only that no HIPAA/BAA mention was found and that there's no HIPAA framework in the trust center.

questions.answer: Tavily publishes no numeric keyless cap. The docs say keyless is free and rate-limited, with limits separate from keyed limits. The SDKs call it a shared rate limit, and a limit error returns code, window, retry_after_seconds and next_actions fields. The CLI calls it a fair-use cap.
questions.notes: Checked keyless.md, rate-limits.md (keyless has 'a different error format and separate limits'), the Python SDK's errors.py, and the JS README; none gives a number. A third-party repo (r12) also says the limit is unpublished. The KB already says 'cap unpublished'.

questions.answer: Reddit filed it. ECF 144 (2026-09-25) is Reddit's Rule 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss SerpApi's counterclaims (Wollmuth Maher & Deutsch; Bartlit Beck). SerpApi's counterclaims (ECF 119, 2026-08-28) plead Sherman Act §2 monopolization and attempted monopolization plus four declaratory-judgment counts. The market alleged is programmatic access to large-scale human forum conversation data for search indexing and AI training/grounding. SerpApi alleges Reddit's 2024-07-01 robots.txt change shut out non-Google crawlers (Bing, DuckDuckGo, Mojeek, Qwant), while Google kept access under a ~$60M/yr deal. It seeks treble damages and an injunction.
questions.notes: I read ECF 144 with curl (WebFetch got a 403) and ECF 119 from the RECAP PDF (gov.uscourts.nysd.651592.119.0.pdf). This confirms the KB's '[inferred] likely Reddit' filer and adds the counterclaim substance the KB lacks. One declaratory count asks for a ruling that no DMCA violation is alleged before January 2025.

questions.answer: Pending on the amended complaint. The court dismissed part of the case on 2026-07-20, and Google amended on 2026-08-10. SerpApi moved to dismiss again on 2026-08-24. On 2026-09-15 the court denied SerpApi's motion to compel Google's licensing agreements, and Google filed its opposition (the latest entry, #58). SerpApi's reply is due 2026-09-29, and the hearing, reset on 2026-09-04, is set for 2026-10-13.
questions.notes: The KB already has this status from the docket. ppc.land's 'September 29 hearing' (r1) was the original setting in ECF 49 and is now stale. Not verified: r1 and r3 say the amended complaint drops the Shopping and Maps theories and rests on three licensing contracts, one of them with Reddit.
